blocks.text: Intro

Already playing. A sweet detuned piano figure over a crooked shuffle: upright bass with string buzz, brushed snare, hollow drum thump, tin-can taps and a loose chain tick. Guitar and muted trumpet exchange frayed little replies. Dry room, rattles, no polish.
Verse 1
Low female alto, warm and casually tuneful. She's entertained, not superior. The ensemble limps charmingly under her; one tap lands late and the others catch it.

Used to be you knew a counterfeit
By the teeth, by the hands, by the light
Now it smiles with a dead man's warmth
And it talks like a Saturday night

You saw the thing and said, "Well, damn"
You let a little wonder through
Then someone said, "A machine made it"
And now you're mad it moved you
Chorus 1
Siren-sweet, hummable hook above a gloriously rattly groove. Piano trips over an accent; bass pulls it back. Tin and chain answer between lines. Teasing, not contemptuous.

You can hiss
You can hack
You can curse the flood
It ain't going back

Get your last licks in
Go on, wear yourself out
The flood don't stop for barking
And it's everywhere now

Take your little swing
Go on, show your fire
Ain't nobody coming to save
Your silly little ire
Verse 2
Guitar slips out and never returns. Trumpet gives a last sour, human-sounding sigh, then disappears. The salvaged percussion stays, quieter. No irony on the mother's voice; let the melody hold.

Don't tell me this is vapor
Don't tell me none of this is real
When your mother's voice comes through the wire
Begging God for a deal

Don't tell me this is progress
Just because the trick got cheap
A polished lie still ruins lives
When it gets in deep
Nearly spoken, plain and sincere. A creak from the piano bench.

You're right about the lie, friend.
You're wrong about the wall.
Verse 3
Piano and rattling bass lead; brushes and tiny found-metal taps weave through the holes. Slightly crooked, never gloomy. This is a confession, not a spotlight.

I never made the brush or paper
Never taught the trees to climb
Every tool came through another hand
Every craft through borrowed time

So what was I protecting, really?
Something holy? Something mine?
Or just a tollbooth in my blood
At the edge of a changing line
Little smile directed at herself.

Don't take the needle personal —
I sang your verses first
I'm just a few floods farther down
And past the part that hurts
Chorus 2
Nothing returns. The piano plays harder, the bass walks with a little swagger, tin and brushes keep the lopsided pulse. Same pretty hook, less teasing. More momentum, not volume.

Truth got thin
Style got thick
You liked it till you knew the trick
And every king with a rented crown
Feels that cold air coming down

You can spit
You can preach
You can pound the table
It's still in reach

Get your last licks in
Go on, have your say
Kick at the future all you want
It's coming anyway

Take your little swing
Throw your little sparks
Morning don't ask permission
It just cuts right through the dark
Bridge
A final metal clank rings out; chain, tin and brushes stop forever. Only spare piano and upright bass, still uneven and alive. On "we" and "ours," her smile fades; not the warmth.

And here's the part that gets me
While we're swinging at the tide:
That little spark was ours to feel
Before we took a side

Right now we still can see the seams —
The teeth, the hands, the light —
We get to stand here certain, friend
Don't blink. Don't blink twice.

'Cause the counterfeit gets cleaner
And the labels wash away
And the next time something moves you
Will you let the feeling stay?
Final section
Piano's repeating figure loses notes and leaves gaps. Bass keeps a worn, patient pulse. No dramatic slowdown. She's thinking aloud now.

Have your little rage
Go on, make it plain
Everybody loves disruption
Till it hollows out their name

Sound it out
Nice and slow
There's no clean way
To watch this go
Bass rattles through one last descending run and falls silent. Piano and voice only.

Get your last licks in
Go on, get it through
The wall came down because it could
And I was leaning on it too

Take your little swing
Go on, show your fire
Close, almost kind. The piano pedal audibly creaks.

Then sit down by the wreck and hold
That silly little ire —
Piano picks at the hook, missing notes. She corrects herself without raising her voice.

Silly, hell. It's certain.
Last certain thing entire.
You didn't fake the wonder.
You didn't fake the bruise.
So cherish it while it's burning —
Confident and true.
Outro
Piano tries the pretty opening phrase, catches on a sour note, then stops. Voice alone, natural and unhurried.

Go on then
Get it out
Morning's here —
The one thing left
Without a doubt
Room tone. No final chord.

notebook.style: Junkyard barroom blues, crooked vaudeville shuffle with a siren-sweet, memorable melody. Weathered low female alto, intimate and warmly melodic; amused at first, then quietly implicated. Never sneering or theatrical. A battered, slightly detuned upright piano plays a pretty repeating figure over a rattling walking bass, brushed snare, hollow oil-drum thump, tin-can rim taps, chain jingle and spring squeak. Scratchy electric guitar and a fraying muted trumpet trade crooked replies. Great musicians on salvaged instruments: loose swing, late clanks, buzzing notes, tiny stumbles and clever recoveries. Dry room, mic bleed, pedal creak, tape saturation, no studio sheen. The song stays inviting as instruments quietly drop out for good, leaving their absence audible. Keep the hook tuneful, never shouted. Last piano figure catches on a missing note; unaccompanied final lines, then room tone. No circus comedy, sinister drones, arena drums or grand finale.
notebook.idea: The song stays inviting as instruments quietly drop out for good, leaving their absence audible.
